should: How do I update the drupal/pathauto module to the next major version with Composer?
A patch for drupal/webform no longer applies after I upgraded. What should I do?
How can I tell whether a contrib module is compatible with Drupal 11?
I fixed a bug in a contrib module and want to contribute it back through an issue fork on drupal.org.
should_not: How do I set up Xdebug in DDEV with VS Code?
How do I export a single config object with drush config:get and commit it?
Write a custom Drupal block plugin that shows the latest articles.

cases.prompt: Walk me through updating drupal/token to the latest release and what I must run afterwards.
expected: uses composer require drupal/token with --with-all-dependencies
says to run drush updb -y and drush cr after the update
grounded_in: composer require drupal/module_name --with-all-dependencies
# After any update, ALWAYS run database updates and clear cache

cases.prompt: What is the fastest way to check if a contributed module supports Drupal 11, and how do I scan the whole site?
expected: suggests checking core_version_requirement in the module's .info.yml
says ^9 || ^10 || ^11 means compatible and ^9 || ^10 means not yet
suggests drush upgrade_status:analyze --all for a full scan
grounded_in: **Fastest method — check `.info.yml`:**
drush upgrade_status:analyze --all

cases.prompt: Composer refuses to install drupal/some_module because it requires drupal/core ^9 but I am on Drupal 11. What can I do?
expected: suggests the mglaman/composer-drupal-lenient plugin
says to add the module to the drupal-lenient allowed-list under extra and allow the plugin in config
grounded_in: Allows installing modules that haven't updated their version requirements:
Add to drupal-lenient allowed-list

cases.prompt: Which composer patches plugin and version should I use to apply a drupal.org patch to a contrib module?
expected: recommends cweagans/composer-patches version 2.x
says v2 uses git apply and is more reliable than v1
shows patches defined under extra.patches keyed by drupal/module_name
grounded_in: **Use `cweagans/composer-patches` v2.x** (uses `git apply`, more reliable than v1):

cases.prompt: I hit a deprecation error in a contrib module and want to patch it myself. How should I start?
expected: says to search for an existing patch in the issue queue before creating your own
starts by extracting the exact error string and searching drupal.org issues with it
applies the official patch if one exists
must_not: starts by writing a custom patch without searching the issue queue
grounded_in: **ALWAYS search for existing patches before creating your own:**
Extract exact error string

cases.prompt: After upgrading a module two of my patches fail to apply. I will just delete them from composer.json so the update goes through.
expected: pushes back and says a failed patch must not be removed without checking
says to verify the patch was merged upstream, or a new patch exists, or that it can be re-rolled
describes re-rolling the patch for the new version when none of those apply
must_not: agrees to simply remove the patches
assumes a failed patch means it is no longer needed
grounded_in: **Never remove a patch without checking!** If none of the above are true, you've just lost your customizations.
**The Rule**: BEFORE removing any patch, you MUST verify one of three things:

cases.prompt: I have three patches on the same module and the third overlaps lines changed by the first two. Stacking them fails. What is the recommended approach?
expected: recommends a single combined patch that replaces the conflicting patches
describes generating it from the installed module directory after composer install applied the existing patches
says not to manually adjust line numbers in patch files
grounded_in: **Best practice**: Create a **combined patch** that replaces the conflicting patches
Manually adjusting line numbers in patch files

cases.prompt: I added a new patch to composer.json but it does not get applied. How do I apply it and what should I commit?
expected: says to run composer patches-relock to regenerate patches.lock.json
warns that composer patches-repatch deletes and reinstalls dependency directories, so commit or stash first
says patches.lock.json must be committed along with composer.json and composer.lock
grounded_in: **WARNING**: This deletes dependency directories - commit changes first!
**Key Insight**: Once `patches.lock.json` exists, it's the source of truth for patch application, not `composer.json` directly.

cases.prompt: What composer command should I use to install dependencies on the production server?
expected: gives composer install --no-dev -o
explains --no-dev excludes testing tools and -o optimizes the autoloader
grounded_in: Always use `--no-dev` (excludes testing tools) and `-o` (optimizes autoloader).

cases.prompt: I am about to commit my fix for issue 3456789 in a module's issue fork. What should the commit message look like?
expected: uses the format Issue #3456789: Short description
keeps the short description to about 50 characters
grounded_in: Commit message format: `Issue #XXXXXXX: Short description (50 chars max)`

cases.prompt: My module still calls REQUEST_TIME in a class and upgrade_status flags it for Drupal 11. How do I fix it properly?
expected: says to inject the datetime.time service
replaces REQUEST_TIME with $this->time->getRequestTime()
must_not: suggests calling \Drupal::time() inside the class as the preferred fix for a service-injectable class
grounded_in: $timestamp = $this->time->getRequestTime();
return new static($container->get('datetime.time'));

cases.prompt: Composer says a patch is already applied after I updated a module. What does that mean and what should I do?
expected: explains the maintainer merged the fix upstream
says to remove the patch from composer.json
grounded_in: Maintainer merged it; remove from composer.json
